title: Resumable stream + tool-call adapter examples (TS/Py/Go) with checkpointing and backpressure
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Current SDK examples assume uninterrupted streaming sessions. Mobile/edge clients and flaky networks cause disconnects which lead to duplicated tool side-effects or lost structured outputs. This ticket delivers SDK helper patterns (TS/Python/Go) that demonstrate: opaque checkpoint token consumption, resumable streaming, client-driven idempotent tool-call helpers, cooperative backpressure (pause/resume), and optional JSON-schema hooks for progressive structured output. The focus is examples and helpers only; runtime API surface remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Three language examples (TypeScript, Python, Go) added under examples/sdk/resumable-toolstream/ in repo
Helpers surface: startStream(), resumeStream(checkpointToken), onCheckpoint(callback), pause(), resume(), sendToolCall(idempotencyKey, toolPayload)
Tool call helper demonstrates dedup key usage with a local cache example and a note about persistence strategies
Backpressure example shows cooperative pause/resume and bounded buffering with clear tradeoffs for memory vs latency
Includes a simple unit test that simulates a network drop and resumed consumption from a saved checkpoint token
Docs PR created and approved by DX; runtime engineer confirms tokens are opaque and supported
decisions: Use opaque string checkpoint tokens emitted in structured progress events by runtime (no new RPC)
Client-driven idempotency: helpers generate dedup keys and show local persisted cache patterns; server-side idempotency recommended but out of scope
Expose JSON schema validation as opt-in to avoid breaking existing consumers
Backpressure implemented cooperatively at SDK layer (pause()/resume()) to avoid synchronous blocking on network I/O
tradeoffs: Opaque tokens improve portability but prevent client-side numeric offsets and fine-grained seeking
Client-side caches reduce duplicate tool execution but add storage and privacy considerations for mobile clients
Opt-in validation prevents accidental regressions but relies on application teams to opt into schema checks
SDK pause/resume increases complexity but preserves runtime compatibility and is simpler than server-side flow control changes
implementation_plan: Finalize helper API and get runtime/DX sign-off (2 days)
Implement TypeScript helpers + web demo that simulates intermittent connectivity (3 days)
Implement Python helpers + CLI resume script (2 days)
Implement Go helpers for server-side resumption patterns (2 days)
Create unit/integration tests that simulate disconnect/resume and verify idempotency (2 days)
Docs PR, DX review, and merge (1 day)
